summary: Retunes one tuple (qkv_gate swap-AB at 17<=m<=32: SPLIT_K 4->8, stages 4->3) in the bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton kernel. Only qkv_gate decode_32 changes, so one run is readable on that row; no companions. No overlap with the pending restack, which never touches the m=17..32 qkv tuple or swapab_ws_qkv.
justification: Arithmetic checks: 24 KB/stage, 3 stages = 72 KB/CTA, 3 CTAs ~219 KB < 228 KB; 16 acc regs/thread; 288 CTAs in 396 slots, one wave; 8-way workspace 2.36 MB. Row 14.2 us vs SGLang 14.6, floor 8.0, kernel 11.8 us (3.2 TB/s), cold L2. Weakest link: the mechanism. Master already keeps ~72 KB/SM in flight, and Little's law needs only ~36-75 KB/SM, so any gain is more likely load balance (144 CTAs of 256 KB on 132 SMs leave 12 SMs 79% over the mean; 288 x 128 KB leave ~24 SMs 34% over). Costs: partial write+reduce doubles (~1.2 -> 2.4 MB each way, mostly L2). Expected ~1.2 us on a 64.5 us load is ~0.3% headline, inside CI: judge on the qkv_gate decode_32 row and its top_kernels time only.
confounders: bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton (landed): retune of its own kernel; the 11.8 us baseline is this kernel on master.
router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m / sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity / router-hilo-at-m8 / bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo: different layers or m ranges; none confounds.
interference: No companion. A control splitting SPLIT_K 8 from stages 3 (e.g. (8,128,4) at 2 CTAs/SM) explains why, not whether; queue only as a follow-up if flat. Restack: no scored-path overlap, a 3-way merge should be clean; if this wins, the same retune is a follow-up for the restack's m<=16 qkv tuple. Sibling o-swapab-m32-splitk2-two-ctas-per-sm edits the same SWAPAB_CFG dict, _swapab_buffers and _swapab_prepare: textual conflict when stacked.
